#lionmama

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A mother defends her child to the death from three armed rapists

Summary:
When a mom in zwartwater, near Lady Frere, was alerted by her daughter's friend that "three men with knives" were raping her daughter she tried to call the police, but got no response. She then went out at 1am to find her daughter She found her in a abandoned house and the men went to for she managed to get the knife off them and then stabbed all three on them. She has been arrested after one of the men died, the other two were inured

Currently she is out on R500 bail and will be back in court on the 8th October

She is willing to do the interview, annymously.

Her daughters friend who told the mother about the rape, was a relative to the boy that died and she has now tried to take her own life as her relatives are berating her for exposing him. It is like what she did by getting him killed is worse than him raping that girl.

Zwartwater village headman Mzukisi Sigqolana said the village was shocked by the incident. But that the village has been quiet since this mother fought back, as these kind of men are a huge problem in the area. He himself has been to the family of three boys to warn them that their boys were making trouble in the village.

Cape Town resident Natalie Kendrick even started a fundraiser online to assist the “#lionmama” or “mother lioness” with legal and counselling fees.
9298$ raised 185% of the initial goal

Press Release:


Lion Mama
In rural communities, sexual assaults are prevalent and women are desperately vulnerable. So what
happens when an Eastern Cape mother defends her daughter against three armed rapists, killing one of
the attackers? Self-defence or an unlawful killing? Carte Blanche untangles the issues.

Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Interview with lion mama Lion Mama: when I got close to the house I heard screams. That's when I went weak. I went into the bedroom where I heard the screams coming from. I came in and I just stood. I saw blankets scattered on the floor. These men were naked. They had taken their clothes off.
2 00:31 Claire Mawisa link to the insert This mother from a rural village in Swartwater in the Eastern Cape is being charged with murder and two counts of assault. After she fought off three men who a legally gang rapped her daughter
3 00:43 Interview with mother and Claire Lion Mama: I heard my phone right. As I answer my phone….

Claire: at night?

Lion mama: at night. As I answer the phone, I hear that it is my mother that is on the line. She says, “there are kids from the village here at the house and they are telling me your daughter is being raped right now by three men in the village”. I phoned Themba Posakwe who is in charge of the police forum of the area.
4 01:36 Voice over of Claire At midnight on the 2nd of September uMama attempted to call the police forum for her village to then her daughter was being attacked but it just kept going to voice mail
5 01:31 Claire link to camera From this village the nearest police station is over an hour away which is a reality for so many communities in rural eastern cape
6 01:40 Voice over Because the police where too far away and not replying to her calls. This mother had no choice but to go and find her daughter and try save her herself.
7 01:51 Interview with lion mama lion mama: I went to my drawer and I took something to protect myself seeing as it was dark. And I know how dangerous this village is. When I was still far from the house I heard screams, that’s when they said she has been crying since 10:00pm

Claire: and it 1:00am now?

lion Mama: it’s after 1:00am now. I entered the door and I had the torch on my phone on. They came at me, you wont believe it . they came at me in such a forceful way. As I was tumbling that’s when I used my weapon . I don't know where he ran off to or how he got out..
8 02:43 Voice over During the fight to proptect hert daughter and defend herself on of the alleged rapists died and two were badly injured at this point memebers of the village had arrived at the scene of the crime.
9 02:56 Interview with Lion Mama Lion mama: I went outside after I finally managed to fight the three of them off. I went outside after I finally
managed to fight the three of them off .
I went outside I found other people standing
there. I told the board’s member to call the
police and ambulance, my work here is done.


10 03:23 Voice over This daughyters life was saved becase her mother got there in time to oprotect her but so many other women in rural eastern cape are not as lucky due to the remoteness of these locations and the lack of police presence, these communities and especially these women are more vulnerable to sexual assult and violent crime.
11 03:43 Lion Mama interview Lion mama: rape takes place a lot here. In
this village there were three grandmothers that were raped and no one got caught
12 04:57 Voice over In all the rural communities of the Eastern Cape there is a system of Governance a board consisting of the Chief, Headsman and Deputy Headsman who are responsible for creating order and keeping the villages safe
13 04:10 Claire link to camera Malibongwe Ntshentshe is the headman of this village and was the first person this mother went to when she got the call
14 04:17 Interview with Malibongwe Malibongwe: I'm in charge here. All the problems that people have they bring them to me. You find cases like people fighting, rape, and stolen good. They come to me an we talk and I find out who's in the wrong so we can evaluate the case

Claire: are women safe in this village?

Malibongwe: we are not safe here. There are a lot of things that take place. We even asked to have a stationed police here to guard during the weekend. We are still waiting and nothing is happening.
15 04:55 Interview with Lion Mama Lion Mama: another lady from here she was raped a few months ago. Her fingers were broken and she cain’t do anything because the person who raped her was a neighbour.

What do you think would have happened to your daughter if you weren’t there?

Lion Mama: I don't know what would’ve happed to my child but something told me that beacause she knew who they were they would have killed her.
16 05:26 Voice over introducing the lawyer One person who is trying to make a different in the Eastern Cape is Buhle, a lawyer and human rights activist who will be representing uMama for free when she goes to trial on the 9th of October.
17 05:38 Interview with Buhle Tonise and Claire Claire: when we spoke to uMama she says that violent crime has increased in the area is this true?

Buhle: that is true, that is confirmed as true. Eastern Cape is quit rural and there are places where by you have to travel 45km on gravel road before you get to a police station. Now in those villages women barely open cases of rape we don't know the exact stats because people choose to keep quiet. The stats show that in rural areas you find that rape cases there's only one rape case reported in probably a month which is not true and we know that its impossible because national stats show otherwise.

Claire: and if she is found guilty what is the worse that would happen?

Buhle: well, remember there are three counts its one of murder which they all have their own minimum sentences so you looking at 15 years to life in imprisonment. However the courts do look at the circumstances surrounding the incident or how crime happened and there's also mitigating circumstances when the court gives sentence.

Claire: what are the young men involved in this case charged with?

Buhle: the other two in the rape case they still have to face those charges and deal with them. When it comes to murder case no remember uMama is the accused so they will be come state witnessed in this case
18 06:55 Claire link When this story broke the #LionMama went viral and one women Nathalie Kendrick started an online fund raising campaign
19 07:04 Voice over Claire q Their goal was to raise $5000 to cover the legal fees but currently they have raised $9373 USD which is 187% more then what they had expected because Buhle has offered to take on the case pro-bono all this money will now be given to the family
20 07:24 Interview with Buhle Claire: why do you think there has been so much media attention with regards to this particular case?

Buhle: I believe its because that humanity dictates that if it was me I would have done the same thing that uMama done. Now that’s why that everybody relates to it, I don't think there is any parent who deserves to see that happen to their child especially when you walk in right in the middle of the act . I don't think uMama will ever recover from that she will carry that uhm memory for the rest of her life

Claire: the fact that a mother had to kill a man in order to protect her child what does ot say about the society we live in?

Buhle: for some reason I don't understand why rapew has become common in South Africa and now people when they talk about it but it seems as though we are not making enough noise and people aren’t really aware of this instance. It’s a sickness, we are a broken society but when you look at the reaction and how many people support uMama it shows that there is still hope its shows that there is still some humanity within us
21 08:23 Interview with lion mama Claire: Ma since people heard this story so many people are supporting you. How does that make you feel?

Lion mama: they make me feel like I have support because a lot of the time I felt like I was alone in this world but when I received the support I felt like I could live again.
